def parse_amount(text):
    # accept decimal dot/comma, spaces around input, zero
    # reject empty, negative and non-finite values with ValueError
    if text is None:
        raise ValueError('None')
    # strip spaces
    s = text.strip()
    if s == '':
        raise ValueError('empty')
    # replace comma with dot if present (only one decimal separator)
    # allow spaces inside? only leading/trailing after strip
    # simple: replace ',' with '.' then try float
    # but reject negative numbers
    # also reject non-finite values (inf, nan)
    # handle zero correctly
    if s.startswith('-') or s.endswith('-'):
        # negative sign anywhere? spec says reject negative values
        raise ValueError('negative')
    # replace comma with dot
    if ',' in s:
        # ensure only one comma and not in wrong place (simple)
        # replace first comma only? but assume single decimal separator
        s = s.replace(',', '.')
    # now s should contain optional leading/trailing zeros etc, dot, digits
    # try to parse
    try:
        val = float(s)
    except ValueError:
        raise ValueError('invalid format')
    # check for non-finite values
    if not (math.isfinite(val)):
        raise ValueError('non-finite')
    return val
